## Summary

`/health` on the MCP server returns 200 without ever touching the ticket store, so a container
with **no store at all** passes both the container HEALTHCHECK and the blue-green readiness
gate. A structurally broken deploy is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:118-120` — the handler returns `JSONResponse({"in_flight": gauge.value})`
  and nothing else.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:56-57` — the container HEALTHCHECK is a plain 200 check on
  `/health`.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:130` — the blue-green readiness gate promotes on that same probe.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:759-761` — the boot sweep is guarded by `if os.path.isdir(_tracker)`
  and emits NOTHING when the store is absent; the comment at `:752` states the intent
  ("a missing store / import / sweep error never aborts boot"), so not even the `debug` line at
  `:769` fires (that needs an exception).

Corroborating log evidence: 60 SSM invocations spanning 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-25 contain zero
matches for `tickets-tracker`, `not initialized`, or `ticket init` — exactly what the code
predicts. (Container logs use `driver: journald` at `docker-compose.yml:72,258,306,383` and no
CloudWatch log group exists for them, so there is no remote log trail either.)

## Why this matters

This is the reason the missing-store defect went unnoticed since deployment. Log-and-continue on
boot is a defensible posture on its own; combining it with a health probe that cannot observe the
store means nothing in the pipeline can ever report the failure.

## How `expected` is computed (the field the whole refusal turns on)

`expected` is TRUE iff the deployment has EXPLICITLY declared where its store lives — concretely
`config.tracker_dir_override()`, i.e. the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` env override is set and non-empty.
It is FALSE when nothing is configured and the path is merely the default relative
`.tickets-tracker` resolved against the repo root.

Deliberately read from the ENV OVERRIDE ALONE, not the parsed config, for two reasons: a health
probe must not be able to fail (or hang) on config parsing, and the repo's
`check_config_ownership` gate reserves `load_config` to approved seams. A project that instead
declares a non-default `tracker.dir` in config therefore reports `expected: false` and simply
does not get the strict gate — it degrades to the pre-change behaviour rather than misreporting.
The deployment surface that matters here (the mcp compose service) sets the env var explicitly.

This is what makes the safety story concrete — and the STATE OF THE BOX MATTERS, so state it
as of now rather than as a standing property. When this was first written the mcp service set
no tracker dir, so `expected` was false and the gate was inert. That is NO LONGER TRUE: the
sibling change kilted-nuclear-bronco now sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`,
verified on the live container. The store is meanwhile absent (a partial clone with no
resolvable HEAD), so the box currently sits at `expected=true, present=false` — exactly the
refusal condition.

The gate is therefore LIVE, not inert, and landing this before the store works would refuse
promotion of every mcp container with `mcp-store-missing`, blocking mcp deploys entirely. That
is the gate behaving as designed; the ordering is the thing that must be controlled. This
ticket accordingly `depends_on` fathomable-yester-thrip (the poisoned-volume fix) and must not
land until a real clone is in place.

## What `present` means, and why it is not HEAD-strict

`present` is exactly `os.path.isdir(path)` — the directory exists. It is deliberately NOT "a
usable store" (a resolvable HEAD), and that choice is load-bearing:

Provisioning is BACKGROUNDED (`provision_store &` then `exec "$@"`) because the ~200k-commit
clone outruns the 120s blue-green readiness deadline. A freshly started container therefore has
a legitimately empty, HEAD-less tracker dir for MINUTES while its clone runs. A HEAD-strict
`present` would report that healthy container as not-ready, the gate would roll it back, and
the next tick would start another — reproducing the rollback loop `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel`
documents. The probe answers "is a store dir here at all", not "is it converged".

**Residual limitation, stated rather than implied:** a POISONED store — files but no usable
`.git`, the state observed in production — satisfies `isdir` and reports `present: True`. This
probe does not detect that and is not the mechanism that should: `fathomable-yester-thrip`
(change 2244, merged) re-clones a store whose HEAD does not resolve. This gate catches the
ABSENT-store deploy; the entrypoint catches the poisoned-store deploy. Neither subsumes the
other, and the acceptance criteria below are scoped to the absent case only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/health` reports the store as a structured object — `{path, present, expected}` — and the
      readiness signal is CONSUMED BY THE EXISTING BLUE-GREEN GATE, not merely present in the
      body. Today that gate treats any HTTP 200 as ready (`autodeploy.sh`,
      `curl -fsS .../health >/dev/null`), so a field nothing parses would change nothing: the
      gate must read the object and refuse promotion on it.
- [ ] The gate FAILS OPEN on an unreadable or malformed signal, matching autodeploy's
      established posture (its in-flight drain check fails open for the same reason: a probe
      that cannot answer is likely a broken service, and blocking deploys on it invents a new
      way to freeze the pipeline). Concretely: a `/health` body that is unparseable, missing the
      `store` object, or missing either key must PROMOTE, never block.
- [ ] The refusal is keyed on `expected AND NOT present`, never on absence alone. A deployment
      that never configured a tracker dir legitimately has no store; requiring one
      unconditionally would refuse a healthy container and take the endpoint down to report a
      non-problem. This is what makes the change safe to land while the box still has no store.
- [ ] The refusal is observable under its own name (`mcp-store-missing`), distinguishable from a
      generic `mcp-unhealthy`.
- [ ] Boot emits one log line naming the tracker path when the store is absent — the sweep stays
      log-and-continue, but stops being silent.
- [ ] `store_status()` never raises for an ordinary resolution fault (a health probe that can
      fail turns a config problem into a restart loop under `restart: always`); the one
      deliberate exception is `RemovedInputError`, which must still fail hard.

## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py -q -p no:randomly
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py -q -p no:randomly

Per-criterion proving tests:

| criterion | proving test |
|---|---|
| gate consumes the field and refuses | `test_storeless_container_is_not_promoted_when_a_store_is_expected` |
| fails open on a body with no store field | `test_health_without_a_store_field_still_promotes` |
| keyed on expected, not absence | `test_storeless_container_IS_promoted_when_no_store_is_expected` |
| named refusal reason | `test_autodeploy_gate_names_the_storeless_refusal` |
| boot names the absent path | `test_boot_sweep_warns_naming_the_path_when_the_store_is_absent` |
| probe never raises / present-store branch runs | `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`, `test_boot_sweep_is_quiet_and_does_not_raise_when_the_store_exists` |

Teeth: gating on `present` alone (dropping `expected`) turns the two promote-cases RED; removing
the gate turns the refusal case RED; an early return in the sweep turns the liveness anchor RED.
